## PFOA Exposure Correlation Network

### The short answer: **Yes, the correlations are dominated by other PFAS compounds** — exactly as you'd expect from shared environmental sources (drinking water, consumer products, food packaging).

---

### 🔗 Exposures Most Correlated with PFOA

Here are all significant correlations with PFOA (|r| > 0.2, Bonferroni-corrected), ranked by strength:

| Rank | Exposure | Description | r | Class |
|------|----------|-------------|---:|-------|
| 1 | **LBXPFOS** | Perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) | **+0.67** | PFAS |
| 2 | **LBXPFNA** | Perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) | **+0.64** | PFAS |
| 3 | **LBXPFHS** | Perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS) | **+0.55** | PFAS |
| 4 | **LBXPFDE** | Perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDeA) | **+0.48** | PFAS |
| 5 | LBXHA | Hepatitis A Antibody (Anti-HAV) | **−0.34** | Infectious |
| 6 | HOQ065 | Home ownership status | **−0.23** | Socioeconomic |
| 7 | LBXPV6 | HPV type result | +0.21 | Infectious |

### 🧪 Among the PFAS cluster itself

The correlation matrix reveals a tightly intercorrelated PFAS block — all 5 legacy PFAS are positively correlated with each other:

| Pair | r |
|------|---:|
| PFDeA ↔ PFNA | 0.71 |
| PFOA ↔ PFOS | 0.67 |
| PFNA ↔ PFOS | 0.63 |
| PFHxS ↔ PFOS | 0.60 |
| PFDeA ↔ PFOS | 0.56 |
| PFHxS ↔ PFOA | 0.55 |
| PFDeA ↔ PFOA | 0.48 |
| PFHxS ↔ PFNA | 0.40 |
| PFDeA ↔ PFHxS | 0.25 |

This is the classic **"PFAS mixture" signature**: these compounds co-occur because they share common sources (contaminated drinking water, fluoropolymer-coated cookware, food packaging, firefighting foam/AFFF). They also share similar pharmacokinetics — long serum half-lives (PFOA ~3.5 years, PFOS ~5 years) and serum albumin binding.

---

### 🤔 The non-PFAS correlations — what's going on?

Two interesting non-chemical correlates emerged:

1. **Hepatitis A antibody (r = −0.34)**: This is almost certainly a **sociodemographic confounder**, not a biological relationship. Hep A seropositivity is a marker of lower SES / immigrant status / developing-country childhood exposure, while PFOA levels track with higher SES (municipal water systems in industrialized areas, consumer product exposure). This is confirmed by…

2. **Home ownership (r = −0.23)**: Renters tend to have lower PFOA — again reflecting the SES gradient. PFOA exposure historically tracked with suburban/affluent water systems near industrial facilities.

These non-PFAS correlations are **much weaker** (|r| ≈ 0.2–0.3) than the PFAS-PFAS correlations (r ≈ 0.5–0.7).

---

### 📊 Key Takeaway

The PFOA correlation neighborhood is **overwhelmingly dominated by other PFAS compounds** (4 of the top 4 correlates, all r > 0.45). This has a critical implication for interpreting PFOA → health associations from ExWAS:

> **You cannot easily disentangle which specific PFAS is driving a health association.** When PFOA is associated with, say, elevated cholesterol, it could equally be PFOS, PFNA, or PFHxS — they move together. This is the classic **mixture collinearity problem** in environmental epidemiology. Any single-pollutant regression on one PFAS is implicitly capturing the effect of the entire PFAS mixture.
